I just posted a reply, but it doesn't seem to have gone through.  Anyway, the short answer is that I don't think the tie issue isn't relevant here.  The discussion of ties is specific to the use of partial likelihood to estimate the semi-parametric Cox model, no?  The survival models included as part of INLA are all parametric.  The coxph model uses a piecewise hazard function, with the relationship between periods characterized by a random walk.  The tell-tale sign that this is not the usual semi-parametric model is the presence of an intercept.  The piecewise random walk is, of course, extremely flexible, thus avoiding the problems that may come with stronger parametric assumptions.  In short, its in the same spirit as the semi-parmetric Cox model, but is not exactly equivalent.

Adam
